attempts.reason_tested: known driver: the axis restates band neutrophils and monocytes
attempts.method: Rank partial correlation of SV-09 axis-2 score (/experiments/SV-09/out/ds05_scores.csv, pc2) with habitus_score (/experiments/shared/tidy/DS05.outcomes.json), residualised on haematocrit, haematocrit squared and log(illness days + 1) as in SV-09, then adding log band neutrophils and log monocytes (/experiments/shared/tidy/DS05.features.json). Permutation p (5,000) and dog bootstrap (2,000), seed 20261112. Script /experiments/SV-META/refutation/scripts/K02_checks.py
attempts.result: Reproduced SV-09: rho -0.257 (-0.408 to -0.097), p 0.002, n 140. Adding bands: -0.167 (-0.313 to -0.003), p 0.049. Adding bands and monocytes: -0.100 (-0.265 to +0.071), p 0.24. Adding all four leukocyte types: -0.130 (-0.280 to +0.018), p 0.12. Total WBC does not explain it (-0.240, p 0.005). Bands alone at a given haematocrit -0.270 (p 0.0008) and monocytes alone -0.276 (p 0.002) are each as strong as the whole axis. The axis-2 link with habitus does not survive control for the two leukocytes already known to track habitus.

attempts.method: Same partial correlation for single red-cell variables and for the regeneration side of axis 2 (pc2 loadings on residualised z of MCV, MCHC, RDW, ARC; also without MCHC), with and without bands and monocytes as covariates
attempts.result: Singles: ARC +0.176 (+0.009 to +0.343), p 0.034; reticulocyte % +0.186, p 0.026 (more reticulocytes, brighter); MCV +0.03, RDW +0.07, MCHC -0.13 (p 0.11), nRBC -0.12: none of these passes. Regeneration side composite -0.170 (-0.315 to -0.019), p 0.042; without MCHC -0.174, p 0.037; after bands and monocytes -0.171 to -0.195, p 0.017 to 0.043. A weak, nominal residual signal that is independent of leukocytes, carried by ARC. It would not pass BH over the census family or over the four checks in this attempt (smallest q about 0.07).

attempts.reason_tested: mechanism: is more inflammation coupled with less regeneration?
attempts.method: Spearman correlation, with dog bootstrap CI, between residualised (haematocrit, haematocrit squared, log illness days) leukocyte counts and residualised ARC, RDW, MCV, MCHC; and between the two sides of axis 2; product term of the two sides against habitus
attempts.result: Leukocyte side vs regeneration side rho -0.002. Unweighted leukocyte sum vs ARC +0.033 (-0.141 to +0.209); vs ARC plus RDW +0.111 (-0.070 to +0.292). Bands vs ARC +0.04; monocytes vs ARC -0.13 (-0.30 to +0.04); segmented vs RDW +0.28 (+0.11 to +0.46). Product term vs habitus +0.079, p 0.34. At a given haematocrit, dogs with more inflammatory leukocytes do not have less regeneration; axis 2 is a contrast created by orthogonality to axis 1 (which moves leukocytes and regeneration together). The named mechanism, inflammation-suppressed regeneration between dogs, is not present in these data; the axis is two independent weak correlates of habitus added together.

attempts.reason_tested: assay artefact: MCHC and reticulocyte arithmetic, haemoglobinaemia
attempts.method: Residual correlation of MCHC with ARC and MCV; axis-2 partial rho after adding MCHC or ARC as covariate; regeneration side without MCHC
attempts.result: Residual MCHC vs ARC -0.41 and vs MCV -0.46: the largest loading (MCHC 0.66) is in part the arithmetic of large, low-MCHC reticulocytes, and calculated MCHC is also raised by free plasma haemoglobin in intravascular haemolysis (not measured in DS05, so not separable). Removing MCHC barely changes the habitus link (axis after MCHC -0.224, p 0.006; regeneration side without MCHC -0.174). Artefact explains the axis shape, not the habitus association.

attempts.reason_tested: confounding: co-infection, illness duration, habitus coding, outliers, fever
attempts.method: Axis-2 partial rho excluding the 3 E. canis PCR-positive dogs (no other co-infection in the 140); adding illness class dummies plus raw days; restricting to illness days <= 7; dropping collapsed dogs (habitus 0); bright vs not bright; trimming the 5% most extreme scores; adding temperature
attempts.result: No E. canis: -0.258, p 0.003 (n 137). Illness class plus days: -0.266, p 0.003. Illness <= 7 days: -0.268, p 0.002 (n 132; only 8 dogs > 7 days). No collapsed dogs: -0.259, p 0.003. Bright (4+, n 9) vs not: -0.170, p 0.036. Trimmed 5%: -0.210, p 0.018. Temperature: -0.242, p 0.005. Not an artefact of co-infection, duration, fever or a few dogs; direction stable.

attempts.reason_tested: already published in a CB article
attempts.method: grep of /core/data/markdown/CB*.md (536 files) for reticulocyte/regeneration with survival, outcome, complicated, severity, habitus; read of matching passages in CB040, CB074, CB082, CB115, CB126, CB129, CB418, CB516
attempts.result: No CB article reports ARC or a leukocyte-against-regeneration balance against habitus or outcome in B. rossi. CB040 (10.1016/j.vetpar.2019.06.005; 320 B. rossi dogs) reports poor regeneration (ARC < 100 in about 62%) but no ARC-outcome test. CB115 (10.1111/vcp.13228) compares ARC with IMHA and controls and over time in experimental dogs (ARC falls about 48 h after parasitaemia), no severity contrast. CB082 (10.1186/s12864-021-07889-4; experimental B. rossi) notes reticulocytosis suppressed as parasitaemia climbed. CB129 (10.36303/jsava.626) shows dyserythropoiesis in marrow. CB074 (B. gibsoni, abstract only) reports reticulocytes correlated with survival (different species, direction not given in abstract). CB126, the article on the DS05 dogs, does not analyse habitus. Not published as a B. rossi severity finding; the mechanism parallel is already made (CB115, CB129).

attempts.reason_tested: tier B eligibility under SV-META spec section 8
attempts.method: Read /experiments/SV-META/spec.md sections 6 and 8 against the results above
attempts.result: Tier B needs a screen pass in one source that is not circular and not a known driver (restates anaemia, band neutrophils or the label). The axis-2 association is a known driver by this test (it vanishes after bands and monocytes). It is one source (SRC-F), already-seen data, with an outcome (habitus) that is soft and owner/clinician graded; the SV-09-03 hard-outcome test restated band neutrophils. The surviving piece (ARC at a given haematocrit with habitus, rho +0.18, p 0.03) is computed here, outside any declared family, and would not pass BH over the census family. Neither part meets tier B.

verdict_reason: The axis-2 association with habitus does not survive control for band neutrophils and monocytes (rho -0.10, -0.27 to +0.07), so it restates leukocytes already known to track dullness, a known driver under the spec. The named mechanism is also absent: at a given haematocrit the leukocyte and regeneration sides are uncorrelated (rho -0.002) and leukocytes do not go with lower ARC. What remains is a weak, uncorrected ARC-brighter link (rho +0.18, p 0.03) in one already-seen clinic file, which could be re-entered as a separate gap/test lead (the DS03-S-CB050 join) but not as K02.

human_counterpart.claim: Serum erythropoietin response is blunted relative to haemoglobin in falciparum malaria anaemia, as in other inflammatory anaemias; proinflammatory cytokines suppress Epo synthesis (Sudanese patients, n 90)

In Zambian children, low IL-10 and high TNF-alpha were associated with severe malarial anaemia and with lower reticulocytes; predictors of severe anaemia differed from those of cerebral malaria (the severity here is defined by haemoglobin, not by consciousness at a given haemoglobin)
Hemozoin-laden monocytes and reduced PGE2/COX-2 are associated with inefficient erythropoiesis (reticulocyte production index < 2) in children with severe malarial anaemia
Hemozoin, TNF-alpha and nitric oxide from stimulated mononuclear cells inhibit erythroid proliferation in vitro
MIF suppresses erythropoietin-dependent erythroid colony formation and MIF knockout mice have less severe malarial anaemia and better survival (P. chabaudi)
DOI 10.1053/beha.1999.0072 suggested in the candidate could not be resolved in PubMed (ID converter returned no record); not verified and not used

canine_parallel_already_made: yes: CB115 and CB129 draw the falciparum-malaria parallel for inadequate or ineffective erythropoiesis in B. rossi (CB082 also notes reticulocytosis suppressed as parasitaemia rises); no CB article links it to clinical severity or habitus
